title: IBM's proposed rule and check assemblies
content:
# Automated Assessment

## Objective

Current OSCAL cDef and SSP models only provide support for a textual description of how a component (s/w, service, process, etc.) implements a catalog control. This may be sufficient for audit documentation requirements as part of an SSP, but does not enable automation of assessments.

Catalog controls specify the requirements at a high-level which are technology/product/service/process agnostic. Each component implements the control requirements in its own way based on the product's design/implementation. What is required is a way to specify how a component implements a control (configuration settings, APIs, etc.) which can then be assessed to validate its compliance.

### User Stories

As an OSCAL component vendor, I would like to specify concrete technical capabilities (rules) that my component provides to support control implementation requirements, which can then be evalauated to validate conformance to specific controls.

As an OSCAL component (assessment tool) vendor such as OpenSCAP, Kyverno, OPA policies, etc., I would like to specify validations (checks) that my tool implements for different component rules. These checks can be either automatically or manually executed and their results (pass, fail, N/A) validate whether a rule satisfies its stated intent or not.

## Proposal

Add support for rules, checks, and related changes to different OSCAL models to help automation of assessments.

### Adding Rules in OSCAL Component Defintion

The product vendors or service providers can specify their product’s compliance implementation by defining the mapping of the regulation controls to the product’s technical policy rules and their parameters. These rules can be thought of as configurations that can be performed on the service, across multiple services, or as behaviors of a product. Since the catalog or profile controls specify requirements at a coarser granularity and are technology agnostic, the rules capture the technology-specific implementation of those controls at a finer granularity such that they can be programmatically verified via checks based on evidence collected programmatically via APIs.

A component provider needs to provide for a given control both (a) the specific rules with related parameters and values, as well as (b) the control responses as text describing how a control is implemented by that product or service.

#### Rule assembly

The below structure gives the proposed rule structure in OSCAL.

- rules [0 to ∞]
  - id [1]
  - title [0 or 1]
  - description [1]
  - audit-procedure [0 or 1]
  - remediation-procedure [0 or 1]
  - params [0 to ∞]
  - evidence-id [0 or 1]
  - props [0 to ∞]
  - links [0 to ∞]
  - remarks [0 or 1]

Each rule will have:

- id: textual id (not uuid) that uniquely identifies a rule in a component
- title: a summary title for the rule
- description: brief explanation of the aspect/objective that this rule supports
- audit-procedure: textual description of how this rules can be validated
- remediation-procedure: textual description of how this rule can be fixed if it is failing
- params: any parameters associated with this rule. These parameter(s) will be used in the validation (check).
- evidence-id: any linkage to evidence data structure or API that is used for evaluation

#### Rule grouping assembly to organize rules

Rules can be grouped to better organize them.

- rule-groups [0 to ∞]
  - id [1]
  - title [0 or 1]
  - description [1]
  - props [0 to ∞]
  - links [0 to ∞]
  - A choice of:
    - rule-groups [0 or 1]
    - rules [0 or 1]

#### An example

```JSON
"components": [
  {
    "uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a985f9",
    "type": "service",
    "title": "COS",
    "description": "COS",
    "rules": [
      {
        "id": "cos_access_endpoint_type",
        "description": "Ensure Cloud Object Storage is accessible only by using {param: endpoint_access} endpoints",
        "params": [
          {
            "id": "endpoint_access",
            "label": "Endpoint Access type",
            "select": {
              "how-many": "one",
              "choice": [
                "public", 
                "private", 
                "direct"
              ]
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "cos_encryption_hyperprotect_key_configured",
        "description": "Ensure Cloud Object Storage is enabled with customer-managed encryption and Keep Your Own Key (KYOK)"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```


#### Rule association to control or statements

Each rule in a component can be associated to one or more controls/statements in implemented requirements. This enables automatation of control implmentation and assessments as the validaiton of a control/statement can now be computed using validation of its associated rules.

- implementing-rules [0 to ∞]
  - rule-id [1]
  - remarks [0 or 1]

```JSON
"control-implementations": [
  {
    "uuid": "08159454-994c-49ed-8f78-f2293b1274a2",
    "source": "trestle://profiles/ACME_official/profile.json",
    "description": "ACME Official Profile",
    "set-parameters": [
      {
        "param-id": "endpoint_access",
        "values": [
          "private"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "implemented-requirements": [
      {
        "uuid": "c6ccfcbc-4553-40e6-b4e8-eadbff8d4756",
        "control-id": "ac-4",
        "description": "This control is implmeneted by ensuring the COS is only available on private endpoints.",
        "implementing-rules": [
            {"rule-id": "cos_access_endpoint_type"}
        ]
      },
      {
        "uuid": "455563ca-c454-41d5-aa3b-f57843d95aab",
        "control-id": "sc-28",
        "description": "Ensure that data is encrypted and the key is managed by the customer.",
        "implementing-rules": [
            {"rule-id": "cos_encryption_hyperprotect_key_configured"}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

### Adding checks in OSCAL Component Defintion (only for components of type "validation")

Policy validation tools (assessment tools) vendors need to specify the policy checks that they implement and their mapping to different products' technical rules. These checks, tests the policy compliance, thus bridging the OSCAL compliance as code into the policy as code.

Please note that we don't capture the actual check code or policy as part of the OSCAL. These will be implemented in their respective policy lanaguages and executed accordingly. We only capture the check ids so that the results (against those ids) can be used to perform the aggregation.

Check defintions are only used to define checks for validation components (assessment tools) and they are not used in other component defintions (s/w, service, process, etc.).

#### Check Assembly (only for validation components)

The below structure gives the proposed check structure in OSCAL.

- checks [0 to ∞]
  - id [1]
  - title [0 or 1]
  - description [1]
  - rule-id [1]
  - target-component-uuid [1]
  - props [0 to ∞]
  - links [0 to ∞]
  - remarks [0 or 1]

Each check will have:

- id: uniquely identifies a check in a validation component. The validation results (pass, fail, etc.) as part of tool execution will be reported against this same id.
- title: a summary title for the check
- description: brief explanation of what this check does
- rule-id: the rule for which this check provides the implementation.
- target-component-uuid: the target component to which the above rule belongs. Rules are only considered unique within a component. Hence, both rule and traget component are required to uniquely identify the rule.

```JSON
"components": [
  {
    "uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a984f8",
    "type": "validation",
    "title": "ANSIBLE",
    "description": "ANSIBLE",
    "checks": [
      {
        "id": "check-1",
        "description": "Check Cloud Object Storage is accessible only by using private endpoints",
        "rule-id": "cos_access_endpoint_type",
        "target-component-uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a985f9"
      },
      {
        "id": "check-2",
        "description": "Check Cloud Object Storage is enabled with customer-managed encryption and Keep Your Own Key (KYOK)",
        "rule-id": "cos_encryption_hyperprotect_key_configured",
        "target-component-uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a985f9"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

### Component Defintion changes

Changes in component defintion structure.

- component
  - uuid [1]
  - type [1]
  - title [1]
  - description [1]
  - purpose [1]
  - **params [0 to ∞]**
  - **A choice of:**
    - **rule-groups [0 or 1]**
    - **rules [0 or 1]**
    - **checks [0 or 1]**
  - ...
  - control-implementations [0 or 1]
    - ...
    - source [1]
    - ....
    - set-params [0 to ∞]
    - implemented-requirements [1 to ∞]
      - ...
      - control-id [1]
      - ....
      - **implementing-rules [0 to ∞]**
      - set-params [0 to ∞]
      - ...
      - statements [0 to ∞]
        - statement-id [1]
        - ...
        - **implementing-rules [0 to ∞]**
        - ...

### SSP changes

Same changes will be applicable to component definition and implemented requirements section in SSP.

One difference to note here is that the component defintion created by vendor will include all possible rules for that component with their association to controls across multiple profiles/catalogs, but when including in the SSP, only those rules need to be selected which are applicable to the SSP (based on the controls in the imported profile). The vendor defined component definiton can be thought of as a library (of all possible rules) and the ones defined in SSP can be thought of as its instance (only including what is relevant).

```JSON
"system-security-plan": {
    "uuid": "7550c0c0-31f9-46fd-b022-3a7ae0f3896f",
    "metadata": ...,
    "import-profile": {
      "href": "trestle://profiles/ACME_official/profile.json"
    },
    "system-characteristics": ...,
    "system-implementation": {
      "components": [
        {
          "uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a985f9",
          "type": "service",
          "title": "COS",
          "description": "COS",
          "rules": [
            {
              "id": "cos_access_endpoint_type",
              "description": "Ensure Cloud Object Storage is accessible only by using {param: endpoint_access} endpoints",
              "params": [
                {
                  "id": "endpoint_access",
                  "label": "Endpoint Access type",
                  "select": {
                    "how-many": "one",
                    "choice": [
                      "public", 
                      "private", 
                      "direct"
                    ]
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
          ],
          "status": {
            "state": "operational"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "control-implementation": {
      "description": "This is the control implementation for the system.",
      "set-parameters": [
        {
          "param-id": "endpoint_access",
          "values": [
            "private"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "implemented-requirements": [
        {
          "uuid": "7ec5da9d-b53a-4030-802d-ad88a49d69d5",
          "control-id": "ac-4",
          "by-components": [
            {
              "component-uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a985f9",
              "uuid": "265e556d-f7c9-4e0d-acdd-48f1e30331ee",
              "description": "This control is implmeneted by ensuring the COS is only available on private endpoints.",
              "implementing-rules": [
                {"rule-id": "cos_access_endpoint_type"}
              ],
              "implementation-status": {
                "state": "implemented"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
}
```

### Changes in Assessment Plan

The validation component can be included in the `assessment-plan->assessment-assets->components`. The check assembly will be included in this component. The original validation component defintion would contain all the checks provided (implemneted) by that specific tool, but when including in the AP, only those checks will be included that are required (same as in SSP for software/service component defintion).

- assessment-plan
  - uuid
  - ....
  - local-definitions
    - activities
      - uuid
      - description
      - **assessment-asset-uuid [0 or 1]**
      - **check-ids [0 to ∞]**
      - ....
  - ...
  - assessment-assets
    - components
      - uuid
      - type
      - title
      - description
      - **checks [0 to ∞]**
      - ...

Validation component and the corresponding checks to be executed (as part of activities) can be associated with `local-defintion->activities`

```JSON
  "activities": [
    {
      "uuid": "a1b2c3d4-1111-4aaa-8888-111111111111",
      "description": "Execute Ansible checks to validate the controls.",
      "assessment-asset-uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a984f8",
      "check-ids": [
        "check-1",
        "check-2"
      ]
      ...
    }
  ]
```

`assessment-plan->tasks` can be used to define when/at what frequency to perform assessment acitivities such as run different assessment (validation) tools - OSCAP for Ubuntu OS, OpenShift Compliance Operator (OSCO) for OpenShift, etc. and which subjects each of these tools perform assessment for. This is done by associating the right activities with the tasks.

### Changes in Assessment Result

Add assessment-check-id and assessment-asset-uuid to each observation to specify the check-id for which this observation is (and for which assest / assessment tool). Also, add result to capture the outcome (pass, fail, n/a).

- observations [0 to ∞]
  - uuid
  - description
  - **assessment-check-id [0 or 1]**
  - **assessment-asset-uuid [0 or 1]**
  - **result [0 or 1]**
  - subjects [0 to 1]
  - ....

```JSON
  {
    "uuid": "6c0a18ff-36b4-45b2-9e8b-6e3011bee6b1",
    "description": "xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_package_prelink_removed",
    "assessment-check-id": "xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_package_prelink_removed",
    "assessment-asset-uuid": "0c410eb1-52cd-40bc-bf1d-c80126a984f8",
    "result": "pass",
    "props": [],
    "methods": [
      "TEST"
    ],
    "subjects": [
      {
        "subject-uuid": "c8ca2d73-c917-4901-9098-71b2c601f471",
        "type": "inventory-item"
      }
    ],
    "collected": "2025-02-26T12:45:58+00:00"
  }
```

## Open questions?

1. AP - Assessment Platform usage? make it optional?
2. AP - Is assessment component sufficient or we need assessment platform also?
3. AP - How is assessment asset associated to the tasks or activities? currently there seems to be no way.
4. In AR there are multiple assessment assests defined. How is an obesrvation associated with an assessment asset? Currently there is no way to do it.
